mcq_fix.s: Which one of the following gives the correct descending order of the following gases in dry air by volume?
mcq_fix.why: CO2 is a variable gas, not a permanent gas; stem was false (y4b6103a7175 asks plain order)

mcq_drop.why: A-R where R merely restates A; oddly worded

pyq_bad.why: wrong options (energy-policy stem with UV options)
wrong topic: physics of radio waves

patterns: APPSC asks one-line facts: N2 ~78%, order N2 > O2 > Ar > CO2, ozone layer in stratosphere, meteors burn in mesosphere, halocarbons/CFCs cause depletion, ozone absorbs UV-B/UV-C
Other PSCs repeat: layer sequence upward, ionosphere reflects radio waves, communication satellites in exosphere, jet aircraft in stratosphere (no clouds)
UPSC adds statement-explanation items: troposphere thicker at equator due to convection; dust more in subtropical/temperate belts
Traps: argon (not CO2) third; meteors in mesosphere not thermosphere; tropopause colder over equator
App leans on multi-statement/match items and 2025-26 current affairs (Mission SANA, ozone hole 2025) beyond PYQ depth
